items.title: Inside an AI‑enabled device code phishing campaign
items.excerpt: A new wave of device code phishing shows how threat actors are scaling account compromise using AI and end‑to‑end automation. This campaign goes beyond traditional phishing by generating live authentication codes on demand, enabling higher success rates and sustained post‑compromise access.

items.title: The Illicit Consent Grant Part 2: Device-Code Phishing and the AI PhaaS Wave | SlashID Blog
items.excerpt: The second installment of the illicit consent grant series examines the convergence of device-code phishing and AI-driven Phishing-as-a-Service platforms. Researchers detail how automated campaigns scale identity theft operations, exploiting OAuth misconfigurations and user trust. Defenders are urged to audit consent grants, restrict device code flows, and deploy AI-aware detection models.

items.title: Device Code Phishing is an Evolution in Identity Takeover
items.excerpt: Device code phishing represents a critical evolution in identity takeover tactics, exploiting the convenience of QR and short-code authentication flows. Threat actors now deploy sophisticated landing pages that silently capture device codes, effectively neutralizing multi-factor authentication. This analysis outlines the technical mechanics, real-world case studies, and defensive controls required to protect organizational accounts.

items.title: Device Code Phishing: Turning a Convenience Feature Into an MFA Bypass
items.excerpt: Convenience authentication features like device codes are increasingly weaponized to circumvent MFA protections. This technical breakdown examines how attackers intercept and submit device codes in real-time, granting unauthorized access without triggering traditional security alerts. Infrastructure teams are advised to review OAuth consent policies, implement conditional access rules, and monitor for anomalous authentication patterns.

items.title: The Device Code Phishing Tsunami: What We’re Seeing in the Wild
items.excerpt: Security researchers observe a massive surge in device code phishing attacks targeting enterprise identity providers. Attackers leverage automated infrastructure to harvest OAuth device codes, bypassing traditional email-based phishing filters. This report details observed TTPs, affected platforms, and mitigation strategies for infrastructure defenders managing modern authentication workflows.

items.title: Device Code Phishing — The Attack That Makes MFA Irrelevant
items.excerpt: Device code phishing has emerged as a primary vector for bypassing modern identity security controls. By targeting the device authorization flow, attackers render traditional MFA mechanisms ineffective. This guide explores the attack lifecycle, highlights indicators of compromise, and provides actionable recommendations for securing identity infrastructure against this growing threat.

items.title: The Shadow Campaigns: Uncovering Global Espionage
items.excerpt: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 uncovers a global espionage campaign leveraging advanced phishing lures and zero-day exploits. The operation targets diplomatic, defense, and technology sectors worldwide. This technical deep dive provides IOCs, attack chain analysis, and defensive guidance for infrastructure teams monitoring state-level threat activity.

items.title: State actor targets 155 countries in 'Shadow Campaigns' espionage op
items.excerpt: A state-sponsored threat group has launched a widespread espionage operation targeting organizations across 155 countries. The campaign utilizes sophisticated spearphishing techniques and custom malware to infiltrate government and private sector networks. This report analyzes the infrastructure, delivery mechanisms, and geopolitical implications of the ongoing operation.

items.title: CVE-2026-72920
items.excerpt: SeaweedFS is a distributed storage system. Prior to 4.24, the filer registers the SeaweedIdentityAccessManagement gRPC service without mandatory authentication when jwt.filer_signing.key is unset, allowing any client that can reach the filer gRPC port to invoke CreateUser, CreateAccessKey, PutPolicy, and related IAM RPCs to mint credentials and gain S3 administrative control. This issue is fixed in versions 4.24.
